root_cause.text: In `spi-sprd-adi` probe error handling, the driver mixed manual `spi_controller_put()` cleanup with devm-managed allocation/registration (`devm_spi_register_controller()`), so a failure in `devm_register_restart_handler()` could trigger `spi_controller_put()` twice on the same `spi_controller`, causing a double free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says the controller was allocated with `spi_alloc_host()` but registered via `devm_spi_register_controller()`, and on `devm_register_restart_handler()` failure the code jumped to `put_ctlr` and called `spi_controller_put()`, while the device core would also call `spi_controller_put()` automatically on probe failure; the patch fixes this by changing to `devm_spi_alloc_host()` and removing the `put_ctlr:` / `spi_controller_put(ctlr);` cleanup path.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says the controller was allocated with `spi_alloc_host()` but registered via `devm_spi_register_controller()`, and on `devm_register_restart_handler()` failure the code jumped to `put_ctlr` and called `spi_controller_put()`, while the device core would also call `spi_controller_put()` automatically on probe failure; the patch fixes this by changing to `devm_spi_alloc_host()` and removing the `put_ctlr:` / `spi_controller_put(ctlr);` cleanup path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use device-managed SPI host allocation to automatically clean up the controller and prevent leaks on error or removal.
intent_record.what: In `sprd_adi_probe()`, the SPI controller allocation call was changed from `spi_alloc_host(&pdev->dev, sizeof(struct sprd_adi))` to `devm_spi_alloc_host(&pdev->dev, sizeof(struct sprd_adi))`.
intent_record.how: This switches the controller allocation to device-managed lifetime handling, so the allocated SPI host is automatically freed when the device is detached or probe fails, reducing the need for explicit cleanup and preventing resource leaks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify the probe error path by returning immediately when resource mapping fails.
intent_record.what: In sprd_adi_probe(), the error handling after devm_platform_get_and_ioremap_resource() was changed from a multi-line block that assigned PTR_ERR(sadi->base) to ret and jumped to put_ctlr, to a პირდაპირ return PTR_ERR(sadi->base) when IS_ERR(sadi->base) is true.
intent_record.how: On failure to map the platform resource, the probe now exits immediately with the mapping error code instead of flowing through the local cleanup path. Because the resource mapping is devm-managed, this simplifies the failure path without changing successful execution, but it skips the explicit put_ctlr cleanup label previously used for this error case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify probe error handling by returning immediately when hardware spinlock acquisition or lookup fails.
intent_record.what: In `sprd_adi_probe()`, the error handling after requesting a hardware spinlock was changed: if `devm_hwspin_lock_request_specific()` returns NULL, the function now returns `-ENXIO` immediately instead of setting `ret` and jumping to `put_ctlr`. In the `default` case of the `switch (ret)`, the code now directly returns the result of `dev_err_probe()` instead of logging via `dev_err_probe()` and then jumping to `put_ctlr`.
intent_record.how: The probe function now exits earlier on hardware spinlock acquisition failures, avoiding the cleanup path used before. Behaviorally, this makes the failure handling more direct and ensures the probe returns an error immediately when the spinlock cannot be obtained or when an unexpected hwlock ID lookup error occurs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify probe error handling by switching to dev_err_probe() and removing redundant manual controller cleanup.
intent_record.what: In sprd_adi_probe(), the error handling after devm_spi_register_controller() and devm_register_restart_handler() was changed from manual dev_err() logging plus a goto to put_ctlr cleanup, to immediate returns using dev_err_probe(); the local put_ctlr label and explicit spi_controller_put(ctlr) cleanup path were removed.
intent_record.how: On failure to register the SPI controller or restart handler, the probe now exits through dev_err_probe(), which reports the error and returns it directly. Because both registrations are devm-managed, the explicit controller put cleanup is no longer needed, so the probe flow is simpler while preserving correct cleanup on failure.

Simplify the probe error path by returning immediately when resource mapping fails.
Simplify probe error handling by returning immediately when hardware spinlock acquisition or lookup fails.

relevance_review.reason: The change switches to device-managed SPI controller allocation/cleanup, which directly addresses the probe error-handling issue caused by mixing manual spi_controller_put() with devm-managed registration. This is related to preventing the double free on failure paths.

The change only simplifies probe error handling for resource mapping failure. It does not address the double-free issue caused by mixing manual spi_controller_put() cleanup with devm-managed controller registration and restart-handler failure paths.

The change only simplifies probe error handling for hardware spinlock acquisition/lookup failures. It does not address the double-free caused by mixing manual spi_controller_put() cleanup with devm-managed controller registration and restart-handler failure handling.

The change directly matches the root cause: it removes redundant manual controller cleanup in probe error handling, which is where the double free occurred when devm-managed controller registration failed.

candidates.rationale: This manual cleanup is reached after `devm_spi_register_controller()` has already made the controller devm-managed; if `devm_register_restart_handler()` fails and the error path also triggers devm cleanup, calling `spi_controller_put()` here can release the same controller twice.

This is the failing operation whose error path jumps to `put_ctlr`; the bug is exposed when this devm-managed registration fails after the controller has already been registered, causing the subsequent manual `spi_controller_put()` cleanup to double free the controller.

Using devm-managed controller registration means the controller will be released automatically on probe failure, so combining this with the later manual `spi_controller_put()` creates the double-put/double-free condition.

vuln_statements.explanation: This manual cleanup runs after devm-managed controller registration, so when the later devm_register_restart_handler() fails and devm cleanup also occurs, the same spi_controller can be released twice.
This is the failing operation that triggers the error path leading to put_ctlr, which then performs an extra spi_controller_put() on a controller already managed by devm.
This devm-managed registration makes the controller subject to automatic cleanup on failure, so pairing it with later manual spi_controller_put() cleanup creates the double-free condition.

diff --git a/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c b/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c
new file mode 100644
index 0000
bic_trace_step.reason: The probe error path clearly shows the problematic mixed cleanup. The controller is created with `ctlr = spi_alloc_master(&pdev->dev, sizeof(struct sprd_adi));`, then later registered with the devm-managed call `ret = devm_spi_register_controller(&pdev->dev, ctlr);`. On failure, the code jumps to `put_ctlr:` and executes `spi_controller_put(ctlr);`. This is the vulnerable construct because devm-managed registration can already arrange for controller cleanup, so manually calling `spi_controller_put()` in the error path can lead to a double put/free if a later devm-managed step fails (as described for `devm_register_restart_handler()`). There is no compensating logic here to avoid the extra put; the code explicitly performs `hwspin_lock_free(sadi->hwlock);` and then `spi_controller_put(ctlr);` unconditionally on the error path, so the fix is not present in this commit.
